summary: Merging the primary question back into a single current interpretation that asserts the defect. Its latest version had become the read-index boundary control, which carries no defect judgment, so a reader taking the latest version as the current account would have seen the finding restated as a boundary observation rather than as the asserted defect it is. The revision covers the whole question in one place: the witness series with the ten receipts and their parsed indices, the flags and running-clock variant, the participant-form control in which an outgoing voter proposes and commits, the admission-on-re-arm observation, and the read-index boundary that confines the harm to the MsgProp entry points. Joint history explains how the lineage receipts, the flags successor, the child control and the read-index boundary share the harness, node set and witness definitions, and states that each cited index belongs to its own run of the same witnesses or to a deliberate contrast case. Counterevidence keeps the source's own acknowledgment that the gate is improvised, the snapshot's expectation that only unknown-leader blocking is intended, the fact that no request is lost, and the four controls that show the effect is neither general nor a mere consequence of any configuration change. Limitations list the earliest receipt's comparison artifact, the Node-API scope, the executed clock schedules and removal forms, the single-instance configuration-proposal and read-index cases, and the contrast with a restarted member that arms the gate when it first learns a leader. No experiment is submitted and no execution is requested.
